Polling for the 17 [[September 2019 Israeli legislative election]]<ref name=dissolved>{{Cite news |url=https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Elections-set-for-Sept-17-after-coalition-talks-fail-591044 |date=30 May 2019 |work=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |author=[[Gil Hoffman]]|author2=Lahav Harkov |title=Israel goes back to elections as Netanyahu fails to form coalition}}</ref> began on 26 May 2019.<ref name=jp>{{cite news |title=New Israeli elections would give Netanyahu an easy win - poll |url=https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Politics-And-Diplomacy/Poll-In-new-Israeli-elections-the-Right-will-get-68-Knesset-seats-590760 |author=Arik Bender |date=27 May 2019 |access-date=28 May 2019 |work=[[The Jerusalem Post]]}}</ref>

== Seat projections ==
=== Graphs ===
These graphs show the polling trends from the time Knesset dissolved until the election day. [[election silence|No polls may be published]] from the end of Friday before the election until the [[polling station]]s closing on election day at 22:00.<ref name=silence>[[s:he:חוק הבחירות (דרכי תעמולה)#סעיף 16ה]] (ח) (in Hebrew)</ref>

If more than one poll was conducted on the same day, the graphs show the average of the polls for that date.

=== Polls ===
Poll results are listed in the table below in reverse chronological order, showing the most recent first. The highest figure in each survey is displayed in bold and the background shaded in the leading party's colour. In the instance that there is a tie, then both figures are shaded. Parties that fall below the threshold are denoted by the percentage of votes that they received (N%), instead of the seats they would have gotten. When a poll has no information on a certain party, that party is instead marked by a dash (–).

== Potential bias ==
Direct Polls institute, which conducts some of the polls, is owned by [[Shlomo Filber]], the former director general of the [[Ministry of Communications (Israel)|Ministry of Communications]] and Likud campaign manager in the [[2015 Israeli legislative election]]. Filber [[turn state's evidence|turned state's evidence]] in [[Case 4000]], in which [[Prime Minister of Israel]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] has been indicted for [[bribery]]. In the [[April 2019 Israeli legislative election]], Filber advised the New Right campaign, potentially compromising his objectivity. Filber's polling method is controversial and is based on [[SMS]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001275500 |title=סמס מעד מדינה: פילבר יחזה עבורכם את תוצאות הבחירות |language=he |work=[[Globes (newspaper)|Globes]] |author=Tal Schneider |date=24 February 2019 |access-date=14 June 2019}}</ref>
